name: Cleavage enhancement tape

card.summary: Skin-safe adhesive tape and push-up taping methods used to lift and gather the breasts for a fuller-looking cleavage under clothing.
card.aka: Lingerie tape, boob tape, fashion tape
card.note: Strong adhesives can cause rashes, blisters or skin tearing.

quick.overview:
Cleavage tape is double-sided or athletic tape used to hold strapless garments in place or to pull and lift the breasts to create cleavage. It gives a temporary shaped silhouette without a bra.

Wikipedia notes that beauty pageant participants and some transgender people use taping to create cleavage, usually by taping under and across the breasts and pulling them together and up.
quick.how: Common choices include surgical micropore and athletic tape, and some people place moleskin under the breasts with tape at the ends. Effects last while worn.
quick.risks: Wikipedia warns that incorrect technique or too-strong adhesive can cause rashes, blisters and skin damage, including skin being torn off.

lead: Cleavage enhancement tape refers to adhesive tape used to hold clothing against the breasts or to lift and gather them into cleavage. Lingerie tape is double-sided and also secures strapless tops and bra straps [1].
Some pageant participants and some transgender people use tape to create cleavage by taping under and across the breasts [1]. Surgical micropore and athletic tape are common [1].
No clinical studies of this technique were found. Wikipedia cautions that strong adhesives and poor technique can injure skin [1].

chain: Tape supports and pulls breasts upward and together
angle.text: Taping creates a lifted, closer-set shape that stays while the tape holds. It is used with garments where a bra would show.

paras: Lingerie or fashion tape is used to prevent wardrobe malfunctions by securing necklines [1]. A cleavage method involves taping beneath and across the breasts, bending forward, and pulling them together and up [1].
Wikipedia reports that rashes, blisters and skin damage may follow incorrect technique or a too-strong adhesive [1].
